metadata.title: AlpacaVision: a curated, licence-audited alpaca detection benchmark, v3.1
metadata.description:
An openly licensed object-detection dataset of alpacas and other South American camelids, assembled from ten public Roboflow Universe projects and audited for licence, label format, exact duplicates, near-duplicates and content: 1,461 images (2,537 boxes) from 517 distinct photographs, single class alpaca, YOLO format.

Version 3.1 supersedes 3.0. Exact deduplication now uses SHA-256 and keeps the licensed copy of byte-identical files (37 files recovered); a content review removed 14 photographs that do not show a live camelid (39 files); and copies that a platform cropped or rescaled are now grouped through the source-photo identifier kept in Roboflow file names. The v3.0 README wrongly stated that CLAHE had been applied; images are distributed as exported. See CHANGELOG.md.

The split is drawn over photographs, not images: train / validation / test = 361 / 77 / 79 photographs (1,035 / 215 / 211 images). On a random per-image split of this corpus, 82.3% of test images have a copy in training, so keep the released split or split by the photo_group column of provenance.csv.

The source projects also label llamas and occasionally wild vicuñas and guanacos as alpaca; the class should be read as South American camelid labelled as alpaca by the source. Every retained image comes from a project declaring CC BY 4.0; per-image provenance and every exclusion with its reason are included.

Code: https://github.com/Andre031222/data-integrity-vision-language-auto-labelling
